subject: Month-end commit check & coaching (action required)
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Month-end commit check & coaching (action required)

Team —

Quick month-end nudge as finance finalizes the June forecast. I ran a quick hygiene pass and flagged a handful of opportunities that need a short re-qualification before we lock commits. Goal: make sure committed ARR in the forecast reflects deals owners are comfortable defending.

Top asks (30-minute task per owner):
- Pull your open opportunities closing in June/July that have had no activity in >60 days or whose close date moved more than 30 days from the last committed close.
- Update Stage (Closed‑Won / Commit / Best Case / No‑Opp) and Close Date to reflect current intent.
- If you're not actively pursuing, set Type=Disqualified or Stage=No‑Opportunity and add a one‑line reason.

I attached a quick CSV with the items I flagged: stale_opps_report_20270603.csv (sample columns: Opportunity, Owner, LastActivity, SFDC Link). Also attaching the commit_review_playbook.pdf with suggested language for customer outreach.

Please update SFDC and HubSpot by EOD Friday (2027-06-04) so finance can finalize the roll-up. Call out any items you want me or Monica to arbitrate in the thread. If you need me to reach out to the buyer directly to re‑qualify, say so and I will.

Quick example of what to change:
- ACME-511: moved to Best Case (buyer confirmed they want to pilot, budget next quarter)
- BRB-227: no activity, please disqualify if you can't reach the champion this week

Thanks — short & decisive updates here will save us a painful re-forecast later.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sales Manager, Mid‑market Accounts
Redwood Inference

Adding a quick coaching note — when you update Stage, please also set Probability and add a one-line buyer sentiment (e.g., "exec aligned, legal review next week" or "no response to pricing request"). That makes it easier for finance to accept a variance instead of assuming the rep forgot to update.

I looked at BRB-235 and Rishi is right — procurement loop will add ~3 weeks, so we should move to Best Case unless procurement emails back with a firm contract date this week.

I'll take BRB-199 and BRB-201 (they're in my patch) and will update by COB Friday.

-Marissa
